brief: Goldman expects Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm majorities to push fiscal-deadline leverage toward limiting the Iran war, rolling back tariffs, and reversing spending cuts; this has already pulled the oil risk premium down, but GS still sees Middle East supply risk re-raising it and lifts its 2027 Brent forecast to $88/bbl (from $80) and TTF forecasts higher, which in turn now points to weaker 2027 European growth (0.9% vs 1.3% previously) and higher peak inflation (2.9%/4.1% vs 2.7%/3.9%). State and local Democratic wins raise AI/data-center regulation risk for utilities and IPPs, though GS expects the issue to fade and any moratoria to be short-lived. On central banks, GS expects the BoE's first hike tomorrow, a second more-likely-than-not in February 2027, but views ~100bp of priced tightening by mid-2027 as too hawkish, and cut its EUR/GBP forecasts. The BoJ's next hike is pulled forward to December on Governor Ueda's hawkish tone, supporting JPY alongside a possible GPIF allocation shift; Mexico may hold, Czechia likely hikes, and PBOC's repo-rate benchmark switch is equivalent to a 5-10bp cut. GS expects Friday's payrolls at a modestly above-consensus 75k, unemployment steady at 4.2%, and AI-displaced workers facing harder re-employment. It also updated S&P 500 and STOXX 600 earnings growth forecasts.
